title: Has anyone tried making a "Dragon's Lair" type game yet? (Branching Story/Playable Movie)
author: New_Acanthocephala62
selftext:
(The video just shows an experiment where I was trying to build a story board builder type of system. Turns out Seedance 2.0 is smart enough to handle scenes directly from the prompt itself)



I want to try to make a simple story based timing/choice game where its like short clips that act as the gameplay and you have to make decisions which cause a whole tree of possibilities to occur (which would increase replay value) with different paths and endings.

The game would be made using generative video and generative images as the main bulk of the game. But of course there could be regular VFX and also possibly game mechanics like typing.

Just curious if anyone has seen a "choose your own story" but with video not just still images and text.

comments.author: DamnageBeats
comments.body: I was trying to visualize how to do one. Your video is helpful

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: Glad to provide some kind of value. Honestly this workflow though isn't really necessary it seems. its good though for humans to map out what exactly the story is comprised of

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I thought about it but it would take too many video generation attempts

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: Yea, I think i've got an angle I'm going to try. a non-human based story. and actually a story where realism is not a part of it. Because realism (lack of it) is what throws it off

comments.author: DerrickBarra
comments.body: Haven't seen this yet, but the current limitations of video generation should be a good fit for this idea. Are you planning on releasing it as a standalone game or streaming it piece by piece?

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: I have nothing to release. I've taken jabs at this concept a few times, but getting the video generation correct is expensive and difficult. I think I've got a decent new plan though on how to make this work.

replies.author: DerrickBarra
replies.body: Yeah no joke, its still less expensive than traditional methods but its still time consuming and still outside of most small/individual budgets. Still your workflow looks nice!

comments.author: PersonOfInterest007
comments.body: Fwiw, the category of game you’re talking about is “FMV” (full-motion video).

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body:
Thank you PerosnOfInterest007. Have you experience experience in this area of the gaming universe?

If you were to suddenly see a successful game in this genre, in your mind what do you think could break through and be a hit?

(plz)

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body:
I don’t have any experience in this. From what I can tell, FMVs are incredibly niche, except in China.

I would say that the only people who should make FMV games are devs who feel artistically compelled to make one. If you actually want to sell a game, this is probably one of the last genres you should ever consider.

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: yea lol i came to that realization

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body: Glad to hear it. Better realize now than a few years into development…

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: Wow I just saw a bunch of youtube videos about this genre. I didn't realize there was already so many of them

comments.author: EmotionalFan5429
comments.body:
I tried it with local model (Wan 2.2) with image to video pipeline.   
1. Generating consistent images was tiresome, but doable  
2. Making Wan 2.2 do exactly what I want was driving me crazy. I have to wait 10-30 minutes only to trash the result time and time again. Characters in videos were doing \*something\*, but they were not acting by the script 99%!

New and way more bigger models like Seedance are more capable, but expect to repeat most of the shots. And expect to pay a lot for this.

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body: Yea. And the part the seduces me is the feeling that maybe if I just figure a different approach it would solve all the issues. Thats why im going to try to not have any humans or realistic things in my next attempt.

replies.author: EmotionalFan5429
replies.body: IMO, all models (unless it's trained specifically on anime, etc.) work better with realistic styles and humans.

comments.author: imlo2
comments.body:
There are a few relatively recent FMV games out there, which have been quite popular and gotten good reviews.

These come to my mind; most notably Her Story which is probably the most popular of this bunch.  
Most of these have received quite good and positive feedback in Steam, and are clearly for a niche of players.

Her Story  
Immortality  
Not For Broadcast  
Late Shift  
428: Shibuya Scramble  
Love Is All Around

Then there are some like "The Isle Tide Hotel" which have quite poor / mixed reviews. But I guess many of the succesful ones are genre consicous games.

And there's a bunch of FMV dating sims from Japan/China etc. which aren't really my thing.

I'd myself enjoy a campy early FMV-era games like Shivers II: Harvest of Souls (where Jason "Metal Jesus" was in a small side role), the really campy Command & Conquer FMV sequences,   
  
Also one sub-genre is the games that mixed sprites and FMV, like a few Star Wars games (Star Wars: Rebel Assault II etc.), so that you had full FMV sequences and also more interactive action sequences with FMV backgrounds.

And there's also some nice use-cases of majority 3D/2D but then as a good accent/realism anchor FMV elements, like the upcoming "I Have No Change" where you're running a night kiosk, which uses 3D background, but actors rendered on billboards which makes a cool authentic feel to a small game.

But there's some interesting opportunities in that space, but for a small genre conscious niche. But there's almost always those 50k people who will love a really bizarre and esoteric game if it's made well...

replies.author: New_Acanthocephala62
replies.body:
wow thanks for this insightful information!  
  
I remember those Command & Conquer cinematics, they really stood out to me back then.  
  
 Yea my goal would be to not try to step on current media formats and just slap AI on it. Ideally this project could be in a category of its own.
